history.summary: Large 1,604 sqft 99LH 3BR at Punggol's Prive for $1.8M / $1,122 psf — the low PSF is partly a function of an oversized unit on a long-lease (2014) project. Pench-of-water Punggol location with only LRT (not MRT) access caps the buyer pool and appreciation versus PDD-adjacent stock.
history.rating_rationale: PSF of $1,122 is genuinely cheap for D19 and the $1.8M quantum sits in a liquid band, but the 1,604 sqft size inflates quantum-per-buyer and the unit relies on Cove LRT (240m) rather than the East-West/Cross Island heavy rail that drives PDD uplift. 99LH from 2014 means ~87 years left — fine — but no URA data was matched here so the appreciation case is unverified. High arena score (744) is largely a value/PSF artifact.

history.summary: Privatised Punggol EC (D19): a large 1,604 sqft 3BR asking $1,122 psf vs verified recent project transactions averaging ~$1,545-1,582 psf — a genuine ~25-27% discount, the largest verified bargain in this batch; the 'very_low_psf' flag reflects real value, not a mis-scrape.
history.rating_rationale: Web-verified: Prive's last-12-month sales averaged ~$1,545 psf and ~$1,583 psf over 6mo, versus the $1,122 psf asking — a ~27% gap. Even applying a meaningful large-unit/big-quantum discount (1,604 sqft is near the top of the project's 775-1,772 sqft range), the implied fair value of a unit this size is roughly $2.3-2.4M, so $1.8M leaves real upside. The algo's age_adj_premium of -33.9% directionally matches my verified read. Now fully privatised (since 2023), Cove LRT ~260m, NEL connectivity, and Punggol's digital-district/regional-centre buildout give a genuine OCR catalyst — the region the v3.4 backtest ranks highest for forward returns. Confidence is medium not high because appreciation_txns=0 and psf_cohort_txns is null (regional_baseline fallback), so I rely on web comps, and the buyer must verify the listing/condition is current (large gaps occasionally signal a stale or distressed listing).
red_flags: appreciation_txns=0 and psf_cohort=null — algo used regional fallback, so verify listing is live and unit condition (a ~27% gap can hint at a stale or problem unit)

history.summary: A 1,604 sqft ground-floor/PES-format 3BR at Prive (ex-EC, Punggol, 99yr from 2010) asking $1.99M / $1,241 psf. The apparent 20% 'discount for its age' is a floor-area artifact, not value: every one of the 6 caveats ever lodged for this 1,603 sqft type at Prive sits in floor band 01-05, and the format structurally trades ~25% below the project's apartment PSF ($1,500-1,670) because the strata area includes a large private enclosed patio. Marked against the only recent same-format print (Sep-2025, 1,603 sqft, 01-05, $1,900,000) and the project's own +2.0% PSF drift since, fair value today is ~$1.94M - the $1.99M ask carries no margin of safety at all.
history.rating_rationale: Avoid for a 5-7yr investment hold: fairly-to-slightly-over priced, weak carry, and a format-specific exit problem. (1) VALUE - the strongest forward lever - is neutral-to-negative once the artifact is corrected. The algo's -20.0% vs the age-adjusted D19 size-band median compares an ex-EC ground-floor PES unit against private apartments; against Prive's own caveats the true comp is the Sep-2025 1,603 sqft 01-05 print at $1,900,000, which marks to ~$1.94M at the project's realized +2.0% drift (core-apartment median PSF $1,562 Jun-Nov 2025 -> $1,593 Feb-Jul 2026). Ask $1.99M is ~+2.7% ABOVE that, and the seller has already cut from $2,188,000 (7 Jun) to $1,990,000 (28 Jul), -9%, without clearing. (2) EXIT LIQUIDITY for this format is genuinely thin: 6 prints in 15 years for the 1,603 sqft type (four in 2018, one 2020, one Sep-2025) versus 95 for the 1,097 sqft and 60 for the 1,054 sqft. The algo's 'very_deep' buyer pool is a 680-unit development read, not a read on this unit - at exit you need one specific buyer who will pay $2.3M+ for a big ground-floor patio in Punggol. (3) CARRY is weak: real IRAS-stamped Prive 3BR rents run a $4,300 median (41 leases, 12mo, range $3,400-$4,900), large 1,300-1,500 sqft units $4,100-$5,300 - roughly 2.7-3.0% gross, not the 3.51% the district_bedroom fallback assumed (conf 0.55); net ~1.6-1.8%. (4) The project's re-rating is DONE: core-apartment median PSF ran $1,270 (2023H1) -> $1,566 (2025H1) on privatisation, then flatlined to $1,593 (2026H1) - +1.7% y/y. Buying the least liquid format in a plateauing project at no discount is negative selection. Region (OCR, realized fwd +3.7%/yr) and the 84-year lease are genuine positives, and nothing here is broken - at ~$1.85M this would be a Neutral - but at $1.99M there is no edge to pay for. The algo's 753 / valuation 92 rests entirely on the mis-comparison described above, and it had zero project transactions to defend itself with (URA's private-condo pull excludes ECs, so ura_transaction_count=0, psf_value=0, txn_volume=0 and age_value +14.46 carried the score).
red_flags: The -20% 'cheap for its age' signal is a PES/ground-floor strata artifact: 6/6 caveats ever for the 1,603 sqft type at Prive are floor band 01-05, as are 4/4 of the 1,722 sqft and all 1,313/1,334/1,388 sqft prints - the format trades $1,073-$1,385 psf against $1,500-$1,670 psf for the project's apartments

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Real evidence beats the model here. IRAS-stamped Prive leases (last 12mo): 3BR median $4,300/mo across 41 contracts, range $3,400-$4,900; 2BR median $3,600 (22); large 1,300-1,500 sqft units $4,100-$5,300. A 1,604 sqft ground-floor 3BR realistically lets at $4,500-$5,000 - tenants pay for bedrooms and floor, not patio area. That is 2.7-3.0% gross on $1.99M (~1.6-1.8% net), against the raw_analysis figure of $5,822 / 3.51% which came from the D19 district_bedroom fallback (confidence 0.55) and is inflated by private Serangoon/Kovan stock. Carry does not compensate for the flat capital picture.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Resale-to-resale, from Prive's own caveats: core-apartment (<=1,250 sqft) median PSF $1,270 (2023H1) -> $1,392 (2024H1) -> $1,566 (2025H1) -> $1,593 (2026H1). The 2023-25 leg was the EC-privatisation re-rating and is spent; the last 12 months are +1.7%. The 1,603 sqft PES format specifically: $1,160,000 (Oct-2020) -> $1,900,000 (Sep-2025), strong on paper but on a single pair of prints in the 2021-26 bull regime, and it has never closed its gap to the 1,442 sqft 4BR (which printed $2.26M Jun-2025 and $2.35M Jan-2026 despite being 11% smaller). Forward I use ~3.0%/yr for this unit - the OCR panel prior (+3.7%) haircut for a plateauing post-catalyst project and a format dependent on a very thin buyer set - versus the 4.2% regional baseline the model applied. Trailing figures are story, not signal.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile for Prive (status: not_researched), so no stack/facing join. The caveat record substitutes for the physical read: the 1,603 / 1,722 / 1,765 sqft types are exclusively floor band 01-05 (11 prints, zero above the 5th floor) - i.e. ground-floor units whose strata area includes a large private enclosed space. Within Prive, the desirable investment formats are the mid-to-high-floor 1,054-1,130 sqft apartments (60/35 prints, $1,600-$1,670 psf in 2026) and the 1,442 sqft 4BR on floors 11-15 ($1,629 psf, $2.35M Jan-2026). Worth a /research-development pass before any further Prive work.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: resale-to-resale only (Prive caveats, propertyforsale.com.sg, updated 29 Jul 2026): core-apartment median PSF $1,566 (2025H1) -> $1,593 (2026H1), +1.7% y/y after the 2023-25 privatisation re-rating; OCR panel prior +3.7% haircut for the plateau and the thin ground-floor PES format
